title: Low-latency delta processor for Console metrics stream
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: The Console currently emits high-cardinality metric points (per-token cost, route-level latency, model-version tags) as full-state updates. Downstream consumers (billing, alerts, realtime dashboards) require fine-grained, low-latency changes but are overwhelmed by redundant full snapshots and suffer from increased egress cost and higher ingest lag.

Proposal: Implement a lightweight delta processor that subscribes to the console metrics raw topic, computes compact deltas (value diffs and tombstones), enriches events with routing metadata (customer_tier, region, model_variant), coalesces frequent micro-updates per key, and emits a compressed, ordered stream to the fanout layer used by billing and the realtime dashboard. The processor will be a stateful stream application deployed as a consumer group with sticky partitioning to preserve per-key ordering.

Key behaviors and design choices:
- Ordering: Use Kafka partitioning by metric_key (customer_id + route + model_version) and ensure the processor maintains local sequence numbers to detect replays.
- State management: Keep an bounded in-memory window (LRU) for recent keys with RocksDB-backed changelog for recovery.
- Coalescing policy: Micro-batching window of 250ms with a max coalesce of 20 events per key to reduce downstream QPS while preserving sub-second responsiveness for dashboards.
- Delta format: Emit explicit {type: "update"|"tombstone", delta_value, prev_value_hash, seq} encoded as compact protobuf.
- Backpressure & fallbacks: If state store grows above threshold, fall back to emitting full snapshots for affected partitions and emit an alert to SRE; provide a throttled mode for low-tier customers.
- Exactly-once considerations: Use Kafka consumer offsets committed after local state persists to changelog; accept at-least-once delivery with idempotence via seq+prev_value_hash to dedupe downstream consumers.
- Metrics & SLOs: Target end-to-end 90th percentile processing latency <350ms and reduce downstream event volume by >=55%.

Tradeoffs considered:
- Flink vs KStreams: KStreams chosen for faster dev iteration and better JVM operator experience with our infra; Flink considered if we need advanced event-time semantics later.
- Strong exactly-once is expensive; we prefer at-least-once + idempotent payloads to simplify operator and lower cost.

Acceptance criteria (must pass):
- Processor handles a simulated traffic profile (burst to 5k keys/s) without exceeding 350ms p90 latency.
- Downstream event volume reduction >=55% on representative traces.
- Recovery from pod restart recovers state and produces no visible regressions in dashboards within 30s.
- Integration tests and a runbook added to the Console SRE runbook.
